## Summary

Show Cloud Sandbox setup progress in the Agents window using the draft session's existing `preparationProgress` surface, shared with local session preparation.

- Preserve repository clone percentages from AHP root project state and show container setup, connection, cloning, and agent-startup messages.
- Reuse the connection's repository-preparation helper and await clone readiness before sending the first prompt and handing off to the real session.
- Remove the sandbox startup chat content provider; no new session provider, temporary chat URI, polling service, or custom progress widget is introduced.
- Cover browser and desktop creation, cancellation, failure cleanup, repository matching, and missing/invalid progress.

## Validation

Passed:

- `npm run compile-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `git diff --check`
- Pre-commit hygiene checks (after applying the repository formatter to the contribution test).

Focused unit tests: **168 passed**:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/cloudSandboxProjectMeta.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts --grep 'CloudSandboxProjectMeta|CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution|CopilotChatSessionsProvider|renders preparation'
```

Changed-file lint: **passed**:

```sh
npx eslint src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/meta/copilotd/cloudSandboxProjectMeta.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/cloudSandboxProjectMeta.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts
```

Live verification on macOS in an isolated Agents window:

1. Enable `chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.enabled` and `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled`.
2. Choose a GitHub-backed workspace, select Cloud, and enable Sandbox.
3. Send a read-only prompt.
4. Observed "Setting up cloud container", "Connecting to cloud container", clone progress at 0%, 1%, and 61%, then "Starting Copilot agent".
5. Verified the real session replied "OK", the transcript contained one prompt, and no files changed.

Browser creation is covered by unit tests; no live browser creation was run.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: First prompt in a new Cloud Sandbox session (default Cloud provider with sandbox enabled or explicit sandbox provider)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The draft now waits for Mission Control task creation, sandbox connection/handshake, repository preparation to reach ready, optional model propagation, and first-turn dispatch. The repository-ready wait is newly on the critical path and can last until the helper's five-minute deadline, but it is the explicit behavior required to prevent dispatch before the checkout exists; progress rendering is local and does not add another remote boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the Mission Control task and on-demand sandbox environment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One task-creation request per accepted first prompt/draft
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same createSession request was already required before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks sandbox creation before connection can begin

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mint credentials, wake/connect the environment, and establish the Web PubSub/AHP connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced attempt per environment address, with existing bounded wake retries and connection timeout
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same connect attempt was awaited before the PR; the diff adds caller-side cancellation racing but not another attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks access to the provisioned session; cancellation now releases the UI caller while the bounded connection attempt may finish in the background

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request extensions/cloneProject when authoritative root state has no matching ready or cloning repository
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when the task-created checkout is already ready/cloning; otherwise at most one request for this first-send preparation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider sent the first prompt immediately after connection and did not invoke repository preparation on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly blocks first-turn dispatch until the checkout is ready or preparation fails/times out

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the first user turn to the provisioned agent-host session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per accepted first prompt
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same first-turn dispatch existed, but happened immediately after provisioning/model propagation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes the handoff to the committed session; now occurs after repository readiness

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical first request per draft. Overlapping sends for the same draft are rejected, connect attempts are coalesced per environment, and repository preparation performs at most one clone request for this call when no matching ready/cloning project is advertised. Progress processing is O(root-state updates × advertised projects), normally one repository and bounded to setup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-draft first sends are serialized by _sandboxSends; CloudSandboxSessionContribution coalesces concurrent connects by environment address. Separate drafts/environments can still provision concurrently as before. The newly invoked preparation has a per-call coalescing map, but this path invokes it once after same-draft overlap is rejected.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A live connection is reused and an in-flight connection is coalesced by address. Root project state is the authoritative warm state: a matching ready project resolves immediately and a matching cloning project is joined without another clone call. A cold/missing project may issue one extensions/cloneProject request. There is no negative cache, but the operation is scoped to one setup attempt and has cancellation plus a five-minute deadline.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the newly ordered critical path and zero-or-one clone IPC because the contribution directly awaits the established preparation helper. High confidence that task creation, connection, and first-turn dispatch were pre-existing boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository clone duration and the frequency of a cold root state are environment-dependent. The changed wait is intentional and bounded; repository progress can generate many updates, but project cardinality is expected to be small and no evidence shows a material CPU or boundary fan-out regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The only substantial added latency is the deliberate repository-readiness dependency required by the change; clone IPC cardinality is bounded and joined against authoritative project state, while same-draft sends and per-environment connects remain coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel sandbox setup while the environment is provisioning or connecting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cancellation now clears the draft preparation surface and rejects the caller immediately through raceCancellationError. An already-started connection continues off the UI critical path until its existing bounded timeout/success/failure, after which the provisioning guard is released.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Continue the already-started sandbox wake/connection after the request UI is canceled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing connection attempt per canceled environment, coalesced for that address
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff the caller remained awaiting the same connection attempt, so the work was not detached and the provisioning guard was released only after the await settled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the canceled caller's critical path; bounded by the pre-existing connection deadline

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one continuing connection attempt per canceled environment because pending connects are coalesced by address. Retained provisioning state scales with simultaneously canceled, still-connecting environments and is bounded by each connection's existing timeout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The base contribution shares one pending connection promise per address. Cancellation does not create retries or additional attempts; it detaches the request while the original connection settles.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pending-connect map and provisioning set retain the environment only during the bounded attempt. Success leaves the normal reusable live connection; failure removes the pending entry and releases the provisioning guard. No indefinite negative cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the new race lets the caller settle before connectionAttempt, and the finally handler retains _provisioning until that promise settles; the service has an existing timeout and per-address coalescing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may rarely cancel during VM wake, and the remaining connection duration varies up to the existing deadline. The lifecycle and bound are explicit in the service.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff improves cancellation latency and intentionally retains a bounded guard so discovery cannot tear down a still-waking environment; it does not add another network attempt or unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display clone percentages and setup messages in the Agents/chat preparation transcript
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Root-state notifications synchronously scan advertised projects, parse matching GitHub remotes, and update one observable progress message; the chat view then replaces the progress item by stable id. This is UI-visible but involves no subprocess, filesystem, database, or network call.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with root-state change count times project count. During preparation there are two short-lived consumers of project state (readiness and progress tracking); tracking self-disposes at ready/failed and the outer request store disposes it on completion/cancellation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates run serially on root-state events. Message equality suppresses duplicate preparation updates, and the tracker is scoped to one active first request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current root state is the warm authoritative snapshot. Repository identity is recomputed on each relevant event rather than cached, but the lifecycle is bounded to setup and project cardinality is small; ready/failed terminal states dispose the observer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the O(events × projects) local CPU/allocation path and bounded observer lifecycle from the added code and disposal branches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact progress event frequency is host-dependent, but percentages are finite/clamped and typical project collections are small. There is no evidence of frame-rate frequency, large collections, or retained history growth.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The repeated local scan is bounded to setup, has realistic small cardinality, and does not cross an expensive boundary or establish material UI jank.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new preparation lifecycle is gated by _usesSandbox; ordinary Cloud session creation continues through the existing chat creation and send path without sandbox provisioning, clone observation, or repository preparation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One request per normal Cloud draft, unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing provider behavior is unchanged because startNewSessionRequest returns undefined and createNewChat follows the previous branch when sandbox use is disabled or not selected.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new sandbox connection, project-state, or preparation cache participates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit _usesSandbox checks in startNewSessionRequest and createNewChat.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed gating path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression on the non-sandbox path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and traced provisioning, connection, clone preparation, progress rendering, cancellation, and non-sandbox gating. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found; the added clone-readiness wait is intentional and bounded, remote operations remain one-per-draft/per-environment with existing coalescing, and observers are short-lived and disposed.
